newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Arianespace to launch Indonesian satellite.
newsitem.headline: Arianespace to launch Indonesian satellite.

text.p: The European space launcher Arianespace signed a contract on Monday to put a Telkom I satellite into orbit for Indonesia's state telecommunications company Telkom PT, Arianespace said.
The new-generation communications satellite, built by the U.S. Lockheed Martin Communications Inc, will be launched in late 1998 or early 1999 from the European spaceport in French Guyana.

Weighing 2.5 tonnes with 36 C band transponders, "the new satellite will enable PT Telekomunikasi Indonesia (Telkom) to offer voice and date telecommunications services for more than 15 years," Arianespace said in a news release.
The contract also includes the training of 10 Telkom staff in space-related programmes in Europe ranging from engineering to economics and law.

This is the third Indonesian contract: Arianespace launched Indonesia's Palapa C2 satellite in May last year and is due to launch an Indostar satellite for the private Indovision television company in July or August.
Arianespace board chairman Charles Bigot declined to give the value of the latest contract, but said the value of the Indonesian contracts so far amounted to "over $200 million".

Bigot told a news conference the Telkom agreement brought to 30 the number of contracts Arianspace had won in Asia and Australia since 1983, the bulk of them in the past seven years. Of the 30, nine satellites remained to be launched.
He said there were "many new directions for space applications", particularly in Southeast Asia. These included direct television, mobile phones and multi-media satellites.
"Asia represents probably a little more than 30 percent of (Arianespace) business in the future," Bigot said.
Customers in the region so far include Australia (the first), India, South Korea, Japan, Singapore, Malaysia, Laos and Thailand.
